title: Lowe’s Supports The Stewpot Dallas With $100K Grant
summary: Lowe’s Supports The Stewpot Dallas With $100K Grant
body_markdown:
Walking into


[The Stewpot](https://www.thestewpot.org/) in Dallas alongside his Lowe’s colleagues, Christian Hall was returning to a place he knew from a very different time in his life.


The Stewpot once offered a lifeline when he needed it most. Now, as


a Lowe’s


associate, Hall had come back to lend a hand to the place that once helped him.


“Coming full circle, helping the people that helped me is, I feel so elevated out of my situation,” Hall said. “I feel like there’s hope now.”


“To me, The Stewpot has been an angel,” he said. “It’s been a lifesaver.”


For more than 50 years, The Stewpot, a ministry of First Presbyterian Church of Dallas, has served neighbors across the city, including people experiencing homelessness and hardship. Its services include a food-choice pantry designed to offer neighbors something simple but meaningful: choice.


Instead of receiving a predetermined box of food, neighbors can select the produce, canned goods, proteins,


desserts


and other items that work best for them and their families.


“Having a food choice pantry means that it’s not just a food box, but people can come in like a regular grocery store,” said Brenda Snitzer, executive director of The Stewpot.


Now, Lowe’s is helping The Stewpot continue


that work


with a $100,000 Lowe’s Community Impact Grant supporting improvements at the organization, including its food-choice pantry.


And Lowe’s associates came to help, too.


Teams gathered at The Stewpot to make 2,000 peanut butter and jelly sandwiches, assemble hygiene kits and paint. Among those volunteers was


Hall


.


“It would be really easy for us just to donate these funds, but it’s so much more personal for us,” said Lowe’s Division President Kyle Lowry. “It’s so much deeper because we show up, our associates roll up our sleeves and we go to work.”


For Hall, showing up was personal.


When Sherrell Washington, a Lowe’s store manager in Midlothian, Texas, began rallying associates for the volunteer project, Hall told her he wanted to be part of it.


Washington soon learned why.


Hall had once been among the neighbors The Stewpot served.


Now, he was returning as a Lowe’s associate to serve others.


“Lowe’s has been one of the most supportive, most positive work environments I’ve ever worked in,” Hall said.


For Snitzer, seeing


someone


The Stewpot once served return as a volunteer underscored the impact the organization can have long after someone walks through its doors.


“Having one of your associates that we’ve been able to help, it shows that it could be anybody,” Snitzer said. “And to be able to help him along his journey is just so heartwarming.”


For Hall, the day brought that


journey


full circle.


The Stewpot had been there when he needed a helping hand. Now, standing shoulder to shoulder with his Lowe’s colleagues, he had an opportunity to extend one to someone else.


“Walking to this room, I was like, ‘Whoa, I never thought I would actually be a part of something like that.’”


The Stewpot has served people experiencing homelessness and hardship in Dallas for more than 50 years. Learn more about The Stewpot and how to get involved


[here](https://www.thestewpot.org/i-want-to-help) .
